author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Google plans to invest at least €13 billion, about $15.1 billion, in artificial-intelligence infrastructure in Finland over 2027 and 2028.

The company said the program will include new data centers, grid improvements, clean-energy projects and battery capacity, Reuters reported. Google described it as its largest single investment in Europe. Finland’s cold climate and relatively low-carbon electricity supply have made the country attractive for large computing facilities.

The commitment adds to a sharp rise in capital spending by major technology companies as they compete to secure electricity, land and specialized hardware for AI services. Alphabet has said its global spending could reach $195 billion to $205 billion, putting pressure on the company to show that higher infrastructure costs produce durable revenue growth.

The Finnish projects will unfold over multiple years, so the announced total is a planned commitment rather than money already spent. Construction schedules, permitting and energy availability can still affect timing. For investors, the development is another measure of how quickly AI competition is shifting from software releases toward long-lived physical assets.
dek: Alphabet’s Google says it will spend at least €13 billion over two years on data centers, power grids and supporting clean-energy projects.
headline: Google plans $15 billion AI infrastructure investment in Finland
